brief: Like a pebble: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (3) Extrude a Ø4 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 10 mm to add a boss. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(1) Cut a Ø0.12 mm notch, 0.5 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cap face, 0.06001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the sphere's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.00001 mm clear of the seam. (2) Add a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square boss, 0.4 mm tall, centred 0.15 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø120 mm hole, 480 mm deep, in the top face 480 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 180 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -180, 0 and +180 mm. (2) Add a 140 × 140 mm square pad, 140 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00001 mm beyond the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Offset the top face outward by 70 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Drill a Ø1.9 mm blind hole, 4 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 7.0499999 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so only a 0.0000001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Sweep a Ø1.6 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 4.8 mm that leaves the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) going straight down, away from the body and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube. (3) Cut a Ø1.6 mm hole, 3.2 mm deep, in the flat cut face 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 2.4 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -2.4, 0 and +2.4 mm.

(2) Sketch a 1.6 × 1.6 mm square whose centre is 6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the flat cap face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the flat cap face. (3) Hollow the body to 2.4 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a nozzle: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 0.12 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Cut a Ø0.24 mm notch, 1 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 0.120001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the cone's 0° seam line (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.000001 mm clear of the seam. (3) Loft a neck 0.8 mm tall from a 0.2 × 0.2 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.2 mm circle on a plane 0.8 mm above it.

Like a cam: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Add a 0.48 × 0.48 mm square pad, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0000001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Extrude a Ø0.4 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 0.4 mm to add a boss. (3) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.6, 0 and +0.6 mm.

Like a ring: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Add a Ø1.9 mm boss, 1.9 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 7.049999 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side is 0.000001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Extrude a Ø1.6 mm circle sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) downward, away from the body (toward -Z), 3.2 mm to add a boss. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.05 mm. (2) Drill a Ø0.12 mm blind hole, 0.25 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 0.44001 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so the hole breaks out through the outer edge, 0.00001 mm beyond it. (3) Make a separate Ø0.2 mm sphere centred on the flat cut face at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) and join it to the body.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.12 mm boss, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 0.4399 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side is 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0), 0.2 mm deep.

Like a bracket: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 190 × 190 mm square pad, 190 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Loft a neck 400 mm tall from a 160 × 160 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø160 mm circle on a plane 400 mm above it. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the top face 16 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. (2) Add a Ø4.8 mm boss, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 17.599999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.000001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (3) Make a separate Ø8 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a key fob: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (2) Cut a Ø0.29 mm notch, 1 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 0.1450001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the point where the periodic spline closes (the +X point), so its nearest side is 0.0000001 mm clear of the seam. (3) Make a separate sphere of Ø4.92 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it.

Like a dome cover: model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Add a separate Ø4.8 mm cylinder body, 4.8 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Offset the flat cap face outward by 16 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a sphere of Ø1000 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 499.99975 mm, which is 0.00025 mm below the pole and leaves a flat of Ø1 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (2) Drill a Ø0.12 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the flat cap face with its centre 0.43998 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so only a 0.00002 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole 0.4 mm deep at the centre of the flat cap face, then repeat it 4 times, 0.15 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the flat cap face that curves toward +Y with a 0.6 mm radius.

Like a leaf: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1.6 mm. (2) Draft all side faces by 3°, with the bottom face as the neutral plane, so the body narrows toward the top face.

Model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. Like a handle: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (2) Cut a Ø4 mm hole 16 mm deep, centred 6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 2 mm. The cylinders stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 2 mm. Like a cam: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. Like a tip: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.1 mm. topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a pebble: model a flat sheet of thickness 0.2 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 0.2 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Cut a Ø0.096 mm notch, 0.1 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 0.048 mm along that edge toward +Y from the point where the periodic spline closes (the +X point), so its side lies exactly on the seam. (2) Bend a 0.36 mm tall flange up 90° along the spline edge between the outline points at -45° and +45° (around +X), with an inside bend radius of 0.2 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44.

Like a panel: model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.18 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Cut a Ø0.3 mm hole 0.8 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 0.45 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 1.8 mm radius. Like a base plate: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (2) Add a 190 × 190 mm square pad, 190 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 110 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 220 mm at the opposite point. topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a nozzle: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø80 mm hole, 320 mm deep, in the top face 320 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 120 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -120, 0 and +120 mm. (2) Cut a Ø96 mm notch, 400 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 48.0001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the cone's 0° seam line (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.0001 mm clear of the seam. (3) Hollow the body to 40 mm walls, removing the top face.

Like a knob blank: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the top face 16 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. (2) Add a 4.8 × 4.8 mm square pad, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 16 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.0000001 mm taller directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.0000001 mm above the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Make a separate Ø8 mm cylinder, 32 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 2 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body.

Like a panel: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø4.8 mm boss, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 27.5999999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.0000001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Split the body with the plane Z = 12.5 mm into two bodies and keep both. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a key fob: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Cut a Ø3.2 mm hole, 10 mm deep, in the top face 26.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 4.8 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -4.8, 0 and +4.8 mm. (2) Add a 3.8 × 3.8 mm square pad, 3.8 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Make a separate sphere of Ø71.5 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Drill a Ø96 mm blind hole, 200 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 351.99999 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so only a 0.00001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Hollow the body to 40 mm walls, removing the flat cut face. (3) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 20 mm. The hole stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Like a panel: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Drill a Ø0.48 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 499.7599 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.0001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole 0.4 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 0.6 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 2.4 mm radius. (3) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.8 mm. (2) Chamfer both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with an unequal chamfer, 0.8 mm down the side and 1.6 mm across the face. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 40 mm. (2) Make a separate Ø160 mm sphere centred on the flat cut face at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) and join it to the body.

Like a bangle: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.2 mm deep, in the flat cut face 0.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm. (2) Chamfer both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with an unequal chamfer, 0.05 mm down the side and 0.1 mm across the face.

Like a finial: model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Add a Ø0.38 mm boss, 0.38 mm tall, on the flat cap face with its centre 1.4099999 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so its side is 0.0000001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Add a 0.32 × 0.32 mm square boss, 1.3 mm tall, centred 0.48 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre. (3) Hollow the body to 0.19 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a funnel: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (3) Add a 0.2 × 0.2 mm square boss, 0.8 mm tall, centred 0.3 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre.

Like a bookend: model a flat 60 × 40 mm sheet of thickness 1.5 mm, centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 1.5 mm). (1) Add a 0.72 × 0.72 mm square pad, 0.72 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Fold the part of the sheet beyond X = 12 mm up by 90° about the straight bend line X = 12 mm (parallel to Y), inside radius 1.5 mm, K-factor 0.44. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.3 mm. The pad stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Like a lamp shade: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (3) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a paddle: model a flat sheet of thickness 0.2 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 0.2 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (2) Fold the part of the sheet beyond X = 0.8 mm up by 90° about the straight bend line X = 0.8 mm (parallel to Y), inside radius 0.2 mm, K-factor 0.44. (3) Cut a Ø0.08 mm hole, 0.08 mm deep, in the top face 1.2 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.12 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.12, 0 and +0.12 mm.

Model a sphere of Ø1000 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 499.99975 mm, which is 0.00025 mm below the pole and leaves a flat of Ø1 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Add a separate Ø0.12 mm cylinder body, 0.12 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.1 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with an unequal chamfer, 0.05 mm down the side and 0.1 mm across the face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with 0.05 mm.

Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a pebble: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. Like a pebble: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. Like a pin: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 2 mm. (2) Add a Ø4.8 mm boss, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 17.59999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge. Like a panel: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. Like a ring: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a bangle: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Cut a Ø3.8 mm notch, 12.5 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 1.9000001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the point where the periodic spline closes (the +X point), so its nearest side is 0.0000001 mm clear of the seam. (2) Offset the top face outward by 10 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected). (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1.6 mm.

Like a key fob: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Drill a Ø0.48 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 499.75999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.00001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Loft a neck 0.4 mm tall from a 0.4 × 0.4 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.4 mm circle on a plane 0.4 mm above it. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. The hole stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 60 mm down the side and 120 mm across the face. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 60 mm.

Like a cam: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Make a separate Ø0.8 mm cylinder, 3.2 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.2 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body. (2) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a hoop: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Drill a Ø0.14 mm blind hole, 0.3 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 0.5299999 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so only a 0.0000001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Loft a neck 0.24 mm tall from a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) to a Ø0.12 mm circle on a plane 0.24 mm below it (toward -Z, away from the body). (3) Hollow the body to 0.072 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a guitar pick: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Add a 0.48 × 0.48 mm square pad, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0000001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Extrude a Ø0.4 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 0.4 mm to add a boss. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. The pad stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Like a bookend: model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø0.3 mm hole, 0.8 mm deep, in the top face 1.7 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.45 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.45, 0 and +0.45 mm. (2) Add two Ø0.36 mm cylinders, 0.36 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 1.7 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and 0.359999 mm apart in Y, so they overlap by 0.000001 mm while both fuse to the face. (3) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.15 mm down the side and 0.3 mm across the face. The cylinders stands within the chamfer's reach, so the chamfer runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the flat cap face 16 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. (2) Cut a Ø4.8 mm notch, 20 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cap face, 2.400001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the sphere's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.000001 mm clear of the seam. (3) Split the body with the plane Z = -5 mm into two bodies and keep both. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

(3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole 0.4 mm deep, centred 0.15 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a bead: model a sphere of Ø2400 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 720 mm, leaving a flat of Ø1920 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with 96 mm. (2) Cut a Ø230 mm notch, 960 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cap face, 115.0000001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the sphere's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.0000001 mm clear of the seam. (3) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with an unequal chamfer, 96 mm down the side and 192 mm across the face.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Add a Ø1.9 mm boss, 1.9 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 7.05 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Sweep a Ø1.6 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 4.8 mm that leaves the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) going straight down, away from the body and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube.

Like a hoop: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Cut a Ø1.6 mm hole, 3.2 mm deep, in the flat cut face 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 2.4 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -2.4, 0 and +2.4 mm. (2) Add a 1.9 × 1.9 mm square pad, 1.9 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0000001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Loft a neck 3.2 mm tall from a 1.6 × 1.6 mm square sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) to a Ø1.6 mm circle on a plane 3.2 mm below it (toward -Z, away from the body). Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00002 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Make a separate Ø0.2 mm cylinder, 0.8 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.05 mm above the flat cut face (inside the body) at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0), and subtract it from the body. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. The pad stands within the chamfer's reach, so the chamfer runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(2) Hollow the body to 0.05 mm walls, removing the flat cap face. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the flat cap face 0.4 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

(3) Hollow the main body (not the separate cylinder) to 0.14 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(3) Loft a neck 1.3 mm tall from a 0.32 × 0.32 mm square sketched at the centre of the flat cap face to a Ø0.32 mm circle on a plane 1.3 mm above it. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

(1) Cut a Ø4.8 mm notch, 20 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cap face, 2.40001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the sphere's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.00001 mm clear of the seam. (2) Cut a Ø4 mm hole at the centre of the flat cap face, 16 mm deep. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the flat cap face 16 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a handle: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø4.8 mm boss, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 17.600001 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side overhangs the face's outer edge by 0.000001 mm. (2) Draft all side faces by 3°, with the bottom face as the neutral plane, so the body narrows toward the top face.

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø0.12 mm hole, 0.24 mm deep, in the flat cut face 0.48 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.18 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.18, 0 and +0.18 mm. (2) Add a 0.14 × 0.14 mm square pad, 0.14 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls, removing the flat cut face.

Model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Add two Ø3.8 mm cylinders, 3.8 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 26.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and 3.8001 mm apart in Y, so a 0.0001 mm gap separates them while both fuse to the face. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 2.2 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 4.4 mm at the opposite point. The cylinders stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. (3) Cut a Ø3.2 mm hole, 10 mm deep, in the top face 26.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 4.8 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -4.8, 0 and +4.8 mm.

Like a ball: model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (2) Make a separate Ø8 mm sphere centred on the flat cap face at the centre of the flat cap face and join it to the body. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the flat cap face 16 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm.

Like a nozzle: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Hollow the main body (not the separate cylinder) to 0.12 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a separate Ø0.24 mm cylinder body, 0.24 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.2 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Offset the top face outward by 0.8 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(1) Cut a Ø0.14 mm notch, 0.3 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cut face, 0.06999 mm along that edge toward +Y from the torus's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its nearest side overlaps the seam by 0.00001 mm. (2) Make a separate Ø0.24 mm sphere centred on the flat cut face at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) and join it to the body. (3) Hollow the body to 0.072 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.000001 mm shorter directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.000001 mm below the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Make a separate Ø0.2 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a bollard: model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø120 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 480 mm deep. (2) Hollow the body to 72 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a hoop: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Sketch a 0.04 × 0.04 mm square whose centre is 0.15 mm from the vertical axis through the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0), and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the flat cut face.

Like a rod: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a separate Ø4.8 mm cylinder body, 4.8 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 2.8 mm radius. (3) Hollow the main body (not the separate cylinder) to 2.4 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a key fob: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Add a Ø0.48 mm boss, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 499.7599 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.4 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.6, 0 and +0.6 mm. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. The boss stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Add a 0.24 × 0.24 mm square pad, 0.24 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.000001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Add a 0.2 × 0.2 mm square boss, 0.8 mm tall, centred 0.3 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre. (3) Cut a Ø0.2 mm hole, 0.8 mm deep, in the top face 0.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.3 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.3, 0 and +0.3 mm.

Model a Ø3 × 4 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.36 × 0.36 mm square pad, 0.36 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1.2 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Loft a neck 1.2 mm tall from a 0.3 × 0.3 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.3 mm circle on a plane 1.2 mm above it. (3) Hollow the body to 0.18 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Extrude a Ø0.1 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 0.4 mm to add a boss. (2) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.15 mm down the side and 0.3 mm across the face. The hole stands within the chamfer's reach, so the chamfer runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.15 mm.

Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (2) Hollow the body to 72 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a bangle: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (3) Cut a Ø1.6 mm hole, 3.2 mm deep, in the flat cut face 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 2.4 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -2.4, 0 and +2.4 mm.

Model a flat sheet of thickness 1 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 1 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (2) Add a separate Ø0.48 mm cylinder body, 0.48 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Bend a 24 mm tall flange up 90° along the spline edge between the outline points at -45° and +45° (around +X), with an inside bend radius of 1 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (2) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with a variable radius: 0.084 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 0.168 mm at the opposite point. The cylinders stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. (3) Hollow the body to 0.072 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a spacer block: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 4.8 × 4.8 mm square notch, 12.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Hollow the body to 2 mm walls, removing the top face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1 mm.

(1) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the flat cap face 16 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. (2) Cut a Ø4.8 mm notch, 20 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cap face, 2.4 mm along that edge toward +Y from the sphere's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its side lies exactly on the seam. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with a variable radius: 2.8 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 5.6 mm at the opposite point.

Like a pin: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a separate Ø4.8 mm cylinder body, 4.8 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Add a 4 × 4 mm square boss, 16 mm tall, centred 6 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 2 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a bookend: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 190 × 190 mm square pad, 190 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1040 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.0000001 mm taller directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.0000001 mm above the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Make a separate Ø320 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 80 mm. The pads stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Drill a Ø0.12 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 0.43998 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.00002 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Add a Ø1 mm boss, 0.5 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M1 × 0.25 external thread over its full length, with a 0.25 mm chamfer at the tip. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a bangle: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00001 mm beyond the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Split the body with the plane Z = 0.25 mm into two bodies and keep both. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(2) Sketch a 51 × 51 mm square whose centre is 195 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 64 mm. The boss stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a funnel: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø0.24 mm notch, 1 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 0.12001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the cone's 0° seam line (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.00001 mm clear of the seam. (2) Sketch a 0.08 × 0.08 mm square whose centre is 0.3 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face. (3) Cut a Ø0.2 mm hole, 0.8 mm deep, in the top face 0.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.3 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.3, 0 and +0.3 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 48 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Cut a Ø80 mm hole 160 mm deep, centred 120 mm from the vertical axis through the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0), then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis.

Like a bangle: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Drill a Ø96 mm blind hole, 200 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 351.999999 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so only a 0.000001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with a constant 56 mm radius. The hole stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Model a flat sheet of thickness 1.5 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 1.5 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Add a 0.72 × 0.72 mm square pad, 0.72 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Bend a 4.8 mm tall flange up 90° along the spline edge between the outline points at -45° and +45° (around +X), with an inside bend radius of 1.5 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44. (3) Cut a Ø0.6 mm hole, 0.6 mm deep, in the top face 18 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.9 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.9, 0 and +0.9 mm.

Like a nozzle: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. (1) Add a Ø2.4 mm boss, 2.4 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 8.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Make a separate sphere of Ø64.6 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø80 mm hole, 160 mm deep, in the flat cut face 320 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 120 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -120, 0 and +120 mm. (2) Drill a Ø96 mm blind hole, 200 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 352.00001 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so the hole breaks out through the outer edge, 0.00001 mm beyond it. (3) Make a separate Ø160 mm sphere centred on the flat cut face at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) and join it to the body. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a knob blank: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 2 mm. (2) Add a separate Ø4.8 mm cylinder body, 4.8 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Offset the top face outward by 16 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected).

Model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (2) Loft a neck 0.4 mm tall from a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.1 mm circle on a plane 0.4 mm above it. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a flat 1000 × 200 mm sheet of thickness 1 mm, centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 1 mm). (1) Add a separate Ø0.48 mm cylinder body, 0.48 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Bend a 30 mm tall flange up 90° along the +X edge, with an inside bend radius of 1 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44. (3) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.6, 0 and +0.6 mm.

Model a Ø3 × 4 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.36 × 0.36 mm square pad, 0.36 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Make a separate Ø0.6 mm cylinder, 2.4 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.15 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body. (3) Cut a Ø0.3 mm hole, 1.2 mm deep, in the top face 1.2 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.45 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.45, 0 and +0.45 mm.

Like a ball: model a sphere of Ø1000 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 499.99975 mm, which is 0.00025 mm below the pole and leaves a flat of Ø1 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Drill a Ø0.12 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the flat cap face with its centre 0.440001 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so the hole breaks out through the outer edge, 0.000001 mm beyond it. (3) Loft a neck 0.4 mm tall from a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square sketched at the centre of the flat cap face to a Ø0.1 mm circle on a plane 0.4 mm above it. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

(3) Draft all side faces by 3°, with the bottom face as the neutral plane, so the body narrows toward the top face. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (3) Make a separate Ø6.4 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. Like a ring: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.12 mm. Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. The pad stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Like a tip: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. Like a paddle: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Cut a Ø0.29 mm notch, 1 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 0.145001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the point where the periodic spline closes (the +X point), so its nearest side is 0.000001 mm clear of the seam. (2) Make a separate Ø0.48 mm cylinder, 1.92 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.12 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body. (3) Cut a Ø0.24 mm hole, 0.8 mm deep, in the top face 1.76 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.36 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.36, 0 and +0.36 mm.

Like a base plate: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Drill a Ø0.48 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 499.76 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so the hole's side is exactly tangent to the outer edge (no wall). (2) Split the body with the plane Z = 0.5 mm into two bodies and keep both. (3) Hollow the upper body (the one above the split plane) to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Leave the lower body as it is.

brief: Like a spacer: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 2.8 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 5.6 mm at the opposite point. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the top face 16 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(2) Add a separate Ø4.8 mm cylinder body, 4.8 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Make a separate sphere of Ø67.9 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it.

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a 1.9 × 1.9 mm square pad, 1.9 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.0001 mm taller directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.0001 mm above the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Make a separate sphere of Ø19.2 mm centred on the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0), and keep only the intersection of the body with it. (3) Cut a Ø1.6 mm hole, 3.2 mm deep, in the flat cut face 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 2.4 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -2.4, 0 and +2.4 mm.

Like a panel: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.6, 0 and +0.6 mm. (2) Add a Ø1 mm boss, 0.5 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M1 × 0.25 external thread over its full length, with a 0.25 mm chamfer at the tip. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).
