(2) Sweep a Ø0.12 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 0.36 mm that leaves the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) going straight down, away from the body and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube. (3) Hollow the body to 0.072 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a key fob: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Add two Ø0.48 mm cylinders, 0.48 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and 0.479999 mm apart in Y, so they overlap by 0.000001 mm while both fuse to the face. (2) Add a 0.4 × 0.4 mm square boss, 0.4 mm tall, centred 0.6 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Hollow the body to 0.072 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Drill a Ø0.14 mm blind hole, 0.3 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 0.530001 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so the hole breaks out through the outer edge, 0.000001 mm beyond it. (3) Loft a neck 0.24 mm tall from a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) to a Ø0.12 mm circle on a plane 0.24 mm below it (toward -Z, away from the body). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a bollard: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square notch, 0.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 0.07 mm radius. (3) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a leaf: model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Cut a 150 × 150 mm square notch, 500 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Loft a neck 400 mm tall from a 130 × 130 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø130 mm circle on a plane 400 mm above it. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Drill a Ø0.24 mm blind hole, 1 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 0.88 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so the hole's side is exactly tangent to the outer edge (no wall). (2) Cut a Ø0.2 mm hole 0.8 mm deep, centred 0.3 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.1 mm. The hole stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Make a separate Ø0.2 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body. (2) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm.

Like a base plate: model a flat 4 × 3 mm sheet of thickness 0.2 mm, centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 0.2 mm). (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.04 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.096 mm boss, 0.096 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1.952001 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side overhangs the face's outer edge by 0.000001 mm. (3) Fold the part of the sheet beyond X = 0.8 mm up by 90° about the straight bend line X = 0.8 mm (parallel to Y), inside radius 0.2 mm, K-factor 0.44.

Model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Drill a Ø0.48 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 499.75998 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.00002 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Loft a neck 0.4 mm tall from a 0.4 × 0.4 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.4 mm circle on a plane 0.4 mm above it. (3) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a tile: model a flat 2400 × 1600 mm sheet of thickness 6 mm, centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 6 mm). (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1.2 mm. (2) Fold the part of the sheet beyond X = 480 mm up by 90° about the straight bend line X = 480 mm (parallel to Y), inside radius 6 mm, K-factor 0.44. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 0.07 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 0.14 mm at the opposite point.

Like a shim: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Extrude a Ø160 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 400 mm to add a boss. (2) Hollow the body to 96 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Hollow the main body (not the separate cylinder) to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a separate Ø0.12 mm cylinder body, 0.12 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.1 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 0.07 mm radius.

Model a sphere of Ø2400 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 720 mm, leaving a flat of Ø1920 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Cut a Ø190 mm hole, 770 mm deep, in the flat cap face 768 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 290 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -290, 0 and +290 mm. (2) Add two Ø230 mm cylinders, 230 mm tall, standing on the flat cap face with centres 768 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X and 229.999999 mm apart in Y, so they overlap by 0.000001 mm while both fuse to the face. (3) Make a separate sphere of Ø3260 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it.

Like a paddle: model a flat sheet of thickness 0.2 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 0.2 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Cut a Ø0.08 mm hole, 0.08 mm deep, in the top face 1.2 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.12 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.12, 0 and +0.12 mm. (2) Add a separate Ø0.096 mm cylinder body, 0.096 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.08 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Bend a 0.36 mm tall flange up 90° along the spline edge between the outline points at -45° and +45° (around +X), with an inside bend radius of 0.2 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44.

Like a handle: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm. (2) Make a separate Ø0.2 mm cylinder, 0.8 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.05 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Model a sphere of Ø2400 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 720 mm, leaving a flat of Ø1920 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with 96 mm. (2) Cut a Ø230 mm notch, 960 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cap face, 115.00002 mm along that edge toward +Y from the sphere's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.00002 mm clear of the seam. (3) Sketch a 77 × 77 mm square whose centre is 285 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the flat cap face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the flat cap face. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a sphere of Ø1000 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 499.99975 mm, which is 0.00025 mm below the pole and leaves a flat of Ø1 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Drill a Ø0.12 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the flat cap face with its centre 0.4399 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so only a 0.0001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Make a separate sphere of Ø1200 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the flat cap face 0.4 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Add a Ø1 mm boss, 0.5 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M1 × 0.25 external thread over its full length, with a 0.25 mm chamfer at the tip.

Like a hoop: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.06 mm. (2) Split the body with the plane Z = 0.3 mm into two bodies and keep both.

Like a guitar pick: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Cut a 3.8 × 3.8 mm square notch, 12.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 2.2 mm radius. (3) Cut a Ø3.2 mm hole, 10 mm deep, in the top face 26.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 4.8 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -4.8, 0 and +4.8 mm. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a flat sheet of thickness 1 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 1 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. Bend a 24 mm tall flange up 90° along the spline edge between the outline points at -45° and +45° (around +X), with an inside bend radius of 1 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a cam: model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Add a 150 × 150 mm square pad, 150 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.000001 mm shorter directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.000001 mm below the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Sweep a Ø130 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 390 mm that leaves the centre of the top face going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube. (3) Cut a Ø130 mm hole, 400 mm deep, in the top face 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 190 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -190, 0 and +190 mm.

Like a tip: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø80 mm hole, 320 mm deep, in the top face 320 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 120 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -120, 0 and +120 mm. (2) Add a separate Ø96 mm cylinder body, 96 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 80 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Add a Ø100 mm boss, 120 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M100 × 6 external thread over its full length, with a 6 mm chamfer at the tip.

Model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a separate Ø0.12 mm cylinder body, 0.12 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.1 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Make a separate sphere of Ø1200 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it.

Like a key fob: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Hollow the body to 0.14 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a 0.29 × 0.29 mm square pad, 0.29 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Cut a Ø0.24 mm hole 0.8 mm deep, centred 0.36 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis.

Like a tile: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø0.48 mm boss, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 499.75999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Add a Ø1 mm boss, 0.5 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M1 × 0.25 external thread over its full length, with a 0.25 mm chamfer at the tip. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. The boss stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a lamp shade: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø96 mm notch, 400 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 48 mm along that edge toward +Y from the cone's 0° seam line (at +X), so its side lies exactly on the seam. (2) Sweep a Ø80 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 240 mm that leaves the centre of the top face going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 40 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a Ø3 × 4 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.36 × 0.36 mm square pad, 0.36 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Sweep a Ø0.3 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 0.9 mm that leaves the centre of the top face going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.15 mm. The pad stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a traffic cone: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Add a 0.24 × 0.24 mm square pad, 0.24 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0000001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 0.14 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 0.28 mm at the opposite point. The pad stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. (3) Hollow the body to 0.12 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Add two Ø0.29 mm cylinders, 0.29 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 1.76 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and 0.290001 mm apart in Y, so a 0.000001 mm gap separates them while both fuse to the face. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 0.17 mm radius. The cylinders stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. (3) Cut a Ø0.24 mm hole, 0.8 mm deep, in the top face 1.76 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.36 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.36, 0 and +0.36 mm.

Like a spacer: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø0.12 mm boss, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.43998 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.00002 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 0.07 mm radius. The boss stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm.

Model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 2.4 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Drill a Ø4.8 mm blind hole, 12.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 27.599999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.000001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole 10 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 6 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 24 mm radius.

Model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with 0.32 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.38 mm boss, 0.38 mm tall, on the flat cap face with its centre 1.410001 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so its side overhangs the face's outer edge by 0.000001 mm. (3) Hollow the body to 0.16 mm walls, removing the flat cap face.

Like a pebble: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Add a separate Ø3.8 mm cylinder body, 3.8 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 3.2 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Cut a Ø3.2 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 10 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 4.8 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -4.8, 0 and +4.8 mm. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1.6 mm. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a panel: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 4 mm. (2) Hollow the body to 2 mm walls, removing the top face.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (1) Add a 96 × 96 mm square pad, 96 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 320 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.000001 mm taller directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.000001 mm above the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Draft all side faces by 3°, with the bottom face as the neutral plane, so the body narrows toward the top face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 40 mm. The pads stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Like a nozzle: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.00002 mm taller directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.00002 mm above the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.4 mm deep. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm. The pads stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a bushing: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø0.12 mm notch, 0.5 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 0.06002 mm along that edge toward +Y from the cylinder's 0° seam line (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.00002 mm clear of the seam. (2) Add a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square boss, 0.4 mm tall, centred 0.15 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm.

Model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Add two Ø4.8 mm cylinders, 4.8 mm tall, standing on the flat cap face with centres 16 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X and 4.799999 mm apart in Y, so they overlap by 0.000001 mm while both fuse to the face. (2) Make a separate Ø8 mm sphere centred on the flat cap face at the centre of the flat cap face and join it to the body. (3) Hollow the body to 2.4 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a bangle: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Loft a neck 160 mm tall from a 80 × 80 mm square sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) to a Ø80 mm circle on a plane 160 mm below it (toward -Z, away from the body). (2) Cut a Ø80 mm hole, 160 mm deep, in the flat cut face 320 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 120 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -120, 0 and +120 mm.

Model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Drill a Ø150 mm blind hole, 500 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 1125.000001 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so the hole breaks out through the outer edge, 0.000001 mm beyond it. (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 64 mm down the side and 128 mm across the face. The hole stands within the chamfer's reach, so the chamfer runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Model a sphere of Ø1000 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 499.99975 mm, which is 0.00025 mm below the pole and leaves a flat of Ø1 mm; the body is the part below that plane. The hole stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a bushing: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

topology: feature at a seam or pole

Like a key fob: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.12 mm. The cylinders stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Like a ball joint housing: model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Hollow the body to 2.4 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Drill a Ø4.8 mm blind hole, 20 mm deep, in the flat cap face with its centre 17.599999 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so only a 0.000001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole at the centre of the flat cap face, 16 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm.

Like a key fob: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(1) Cut a Ø0.29 mm notch, 1 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 0.1450001 mm along that edge toward +Y from the point where the periodic spline closes (the +X point), so its nearest side is 0.0000001 mm clear of the seam. (2) Make a separate Ø0.48 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body.

Model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Cut a 150 × 150 mm square notch, 500 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Split the body with the plane Z = 500 mm into two bodies and keep both. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face on the upper body (the one with the original top face) with 64 mm.

Like a bead: model a sphere of Ø2400 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 720 mm, leaving a flat of Ø1920 mm; the body is the part below that plane. Offset the flat cap face outward by 770 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add two Ø0.12 mm cylinders, 0.12 mm tall, standing on the flat cut face with centres 0.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X and 0.119999 mm apart in Y, so they overlap by 0.000001 mm while both fuse to the face. (2) Add a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square boss, 0.2 mm tall, centred 0.15 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre. (3) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Make a separate Ø8 mm cylinder, 32 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 2 mm below the flat cap face at the centre of the flat cap face, and subtract it from the body. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with 2 mm.

Model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 60 mm. (2) Sketch a 48 × 48 mm square whose centre is 180 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face.

Like a bushing: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square notch, 0.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Loft a neck 0.4 mm tall from a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.1 mm circle on a plane 0.4 mm above it. (3) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Add two Ø150 mm cylinders, 150 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and 150 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 90 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 180 mm at the opposite point. The cylinders stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. (3) Cut a Ø130 mm hole, 400 mm deep, in the top face 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 190 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -190, 0 and +190 mm.

Like a hoop: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a separate Ø0.12 mm cylinder body, 0.12 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.1 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole 0.2 mm deep, centred 0.15 mm from the vertical axis through the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0), then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a pebble: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1.6 mm. (2) Add a 3.8 × 3.8 mm square pad, 3.8 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 26.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.00002 mm taller directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.00002 mm above the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Make a separate Ø6.4 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body.

Like a spacer block: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 96 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Drill a Ø190 mm blind hole, 500 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 1104.9999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.0001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Split the body with the plane Z = 500 mm into two bodies and keep both.

Like a bracket: model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. Cut a Ø0.3 mm hole 0.8 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 0.45 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 1.8 mm radius. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add two Ø1.9 mm cylinders, 1.9 mm tall, standing on the flat cut face with centres 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X and 1.9000001 mm apart in Y, so a 0.0000001 mm gap separates them while both fuse to the face. (2) Hollow the body to 0.8 mm walls, removing the flat cut face. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Add a Ø0.48 mm boss, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 499.75999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.4 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.6, 0 and +0.6 mm. (3) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a flat sheet of thickness 0.2 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 0.2 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.04 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.096 mm boss, 0.096 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1.95198 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.00002 mm inside the face's outer edge. (3) Bend a 0.36 mm tall flange up 90° along the spline edge between the outline points at -45° and +45° (around +X), with an inside bend radius of 0.2 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44.

Like a cam: model a flat sheet of thickness 1.5 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin in X and Y, with its bottom face on Z = 0 (it fills Z = 0 to 1.5 mm) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Cut a 0.72 × 0.72 mm square notch, 0.75 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Bend a 4.8 mm tall flange up 90° along the spline edge between the outline points at -45° and +45° (around +X), with an inside bend radius of 1.5 mm (the thickness) and a K-factor of 0.44. (3) Cut a Ø0.6 mm hole, 0.6 mm deep, in the top face 18 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.9 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.9, 0 and +0.9 mm.

Like a traffic cone: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø0.2 mm hole, 0.8 mm deep, in the top face 0.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.3 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.3, 0 and +0.3 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.24 mm boss, 0.24 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.87999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (3) Make a separate Ø0.4 mm cylinder, 1.6 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.1 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body.

Model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 0.07 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 0.14 mm at the opposite point. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00002 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0), 0.2 mm deep.

Like a spacer block: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 10 mm deep, in the top face 26 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. (2) Cut a 4.8 × 4.8 mm square notch, 12.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (3) Make a separate Ø8 mm cylinder, 32 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 2 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305); then move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a hoop: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.8 mm. (2) Add a Ø1.9 mm boss, 1.9 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 7.05001 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side overhangs the face's outer edge by 0.00001 mm. (3) Offset the flat cut face outward by 0.95 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a label plate: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.6, 0 and +0.6 mm. (2) Drill a Ø0.48 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 499.7599999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.0000001 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Add a Ø1 mm boss, 0.5 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M1 × 0.25 external thread over its full length, with a 0.25 mm chamfer at the tip.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø0.14 mm boss, 0.14 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 0.5299 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side is 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (2) Sketch a 0.048 × 0.048 mm square whose centre is 0.18 mm from the vertical axis through the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0), and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the flat cut face. (3) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.06 mm. The boss stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Cut a Ø96 mm notch, 200 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the flat cut face, 48.00002 mm along that edge toward +Y from the torus's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so its nearest side is 0.00002 mm clear of the seam. (2) Extrude a Ø80 mm circle sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) downward, away from the body (toward -Z), 160 mm to add a boss. (3) Hollow the body to 48 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a shim: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.48 × 0.48 mm square pad, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.00001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Sweep a Ø0.4 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 1.2 mm that leaves the centre of the top face going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. The pad stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built.

Like a panel: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 10 mm deep, in the top face 26 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -6, 0 and +6 mm. (2) Add a Ø4.8 mm boss, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 27.599999 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is 0.000001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 2.8 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 5.6 mm at the opposite point. The boss stands within the fillet's reach, so the fillet runs into it: round the edge up to it, or refuse if that cannot be built. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0 (the flat face faces down, toward -Z, and the body lies above it). (1) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 0.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, and a second pad of the same footprint that is 0.000001 mm taller directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so its top sits 0.000001 mm above the first pad's top and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Loft a neck 0.2 mm tall from a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) to a Ø0.1 mm circle on a plane 0.2 mm below it (toward -Z, away from the body). (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.2 mm deep, in the flat cut face 0.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch, so the holes are at Y = -0.15, 0 and +0.15 mm.

Model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Add a separate Ø0.29 mm cylinder body, 0.29 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.24 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.12 mm down the side and 0.24 mm across the face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.12 mm.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø4.8 mm notch, 20 mm deep, centred on the outer edge of the top face, 2.399999 mm along that edge toward +Y from the cylinder's 0° seam line (at +X), so its nearest side overlaps the seam by 0.000001 mm. (2) Make a separate Ø8 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body. (3) Hollow the body to 2.4 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

(2) Make a separate sphere of Ø1200 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it. (2) Chamfer both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with an unequal chamfer, 0.8 mm down the side and 1.6 mm across the face. Finally, rotate everything 17° about X, then 31° about Z, both through the origin (right-hand rule): the original X axis then points along (0.857167, 0.515038, 0) and the original Z axis along (0.150583, -0.250611, 0.956305).

Like a shim: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 96 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a 190 × 190 mm square pad, 190 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Cut a Ø160 mm hole 400 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 240 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 960 mm radius.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.06 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.14 mm boss, 0.14 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 0.5299 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side is 0.0001 mm inside the face's outer edge. (3) Make a separate Ø0.24 mm sphere centred on the flat cut face at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) and join it to the body. Finally, move everything 10000 mm along +X: the original origin lands at (10000, 0, 0).

Model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)].
